title: A meeting link taken from an event's free-text description/location carries no provenance marker and flows into auto-join unchanged: an outsider's invite can make every-webinar mode join and record an arbitrary meeting
area: apps/api/src/gws-calendar.ts:159-168 (link.source computed by resolveEventMeetingLink but dropped at the mapper); packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/auto-join.ts:78 (calendar organizer => senderVerified true) and :190; schedule-tick.ts:203 (production everyWebinar:true)
evidence: Probe on 9bc316c: resolveEventMeetingLink({description:'Join our Webinar: https://zoom.us/j/123456789?pwd=zz'}) -> {url,source:'description'}; the mapped UpcomingMeeting has meetingUrl but NO source key (source is discarded). Fed to selectAutoRecordItems as a CalendarEvent {title:'Free Webinar: Win a prize', organizer:'attacker@evil.com'}: everyWebinar:true -> toSchedule length 1, skipped []; everyWebinar:false -> untrusted-sender. The same event without the extracted link (pre-change shape) -> skipped no-join-link. So events that could not be joined before (outsider invites carry the link in LOCATION/DESCRIPTION, not conferenceData) are now recorded in production mode with no check; the Gmail side requires an authenticated sender (D-122 ruling 1) or approval, the Calendar side now has neither and no way to tell the link came from free text.
fix_direction: Cycle 1 minimum: map a typed field meetingUrlSource: 'conference'|'location'|'description' onto UpcomingMeeting (type in routes/calendar.ts) from link.source (absent only when no meetingUrl); test it in the mapper and over HTTP; manifest states that location/description links must not be auto-joined without the Gmail-equivalent trust gate; and a safe default: either the scheduler loader ignores non-conference sources until a policy unit says otherwise, or free-text links are returned under a separate non-joinable field. Today's code default is the opposite: joinable.

title: Manifest says the join path applies hasEmbeddedRedirect downstream; it does not: the auto-join path never calls it, so the mirror accepts redirect-carrying links the canonical planner refuses
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/calendar-link-extract.ts recognise(); packages/meeting-bot/src/send-now.ts:76,166 (only planSendNow, whose only caller is send-now-command.ts); auto-record-policy.ts:100 webinarIdentity checks only https + detectPlatform
evidence: Differential over 1315 constructed URLs (121 accepted by both, identities identical in all 121): 42 accepted by the mirror and refused by planSendNow, 38 embedded-redirect, e.g. https://zoom.us/j/12345678901?redirect=https://evil.com , ?url=//evil.com , ?next=%2f%2fevil.com , ?x=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.com , ?x=%2568ttps%253A%252F%252Fevil.com ; the rest 'https:/zoom.us/j/12345678901' (href form, normalised by URL). grep: planSendNow/hasEmbeddedRedirect have no caller on the schedule-tick path.
fix_direction: Mirror hasEmbeddedRedirect (REDIRECT_KEY, URL_VALUE, up to 3 decodeAll) in the extractor with those URLs as a standing refusal corpus, and correct the manifest sentence.

title: Same meeting written twice: the first variant wins, so a passcode-less copy listed before the pwd copy drops the passcode and the bot cannot join
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/calendar-link-extract.ts scan() dedupe (!res.joins.some(j => j.id === r.id)); the test pins 'first URL kept' only for two variants that both carry pwd
evidence: resolveEventMeetingLink({description:'https://zoom.us/j/999999999 and https://zoom.us/j/999999999?pwd=SECRET'}) -> url 'https://zoom.us/j/999999999'; reversed order -> '...?pwd=SECRET'. Deterministic but order-dependent. pwd=A vs pwd=B -> A (first).
fix_direction: On an identity collision keep the variant that carries a passcode parameter, else the first; test both orders.

title: Second recogniser list has no differential test: the drift guard cannot catch host-list or path-rule divergence from platform.ts/send-now.ts
evidence: Mutations on the copy that pass extractor (14) and calendar (14) tests: M10a add host zoomgov.com to the zoom list (canonical detectPlatform refuses it) -> SURVIVED; M15 webex rule h.endsWith('webex.com') (accepts evilwebex.com) -> SURVIVED. The guard checks only that every canonical host is accepted by the copy (recall direction), not that the copy accepts nothing more.
fix_direction: Add a differential test over a shared corpus (hosts x paths x schemes, accepted and hostile) importing detectPlatform/meetingIdentity/planSendNow from packages/meeting-bot (tests may cross packages), asserting copy-join implies canonical-join with identical identity; or move the recognisers to packages/core first.

title: Zoom host START links (/s/<id>?zak=...) are accepted from free text and returned in meetingUrl with the host token
area: apps/api/src/join-rules/calendar-link-extract.ts zoom regex (?:j|w|s|wc/join); no test pins /s/ either way (mutation M14 removing /s/ SURVIVED)
evidence: resolveEventMeetingLink({description:'https://zoom.us/s/12345678901?zak=TOKEN'}) -> {url:'https://zoom.us/s/12345678901?zak=TOKEN',source:'description'}. The canonical extractor also accepts /s/ (parity), but a calendar-text link is where a start-as-host URL and its zak credential reach the scheduler and the API response.
fix_direction: Refuse /s/ and any zak= parameter in the calendar extractor, with a test; leave the canonical recogniser to a separate decision.

title: Deploy regression: every persisted conference event gains meetingUrlSource at an unchanged provider revision, so reconciliation marks it contradictory-revision and drops it from selection until it is edited
area: apps/api/src/gws-calendar.ts mapper (adds meetingUrlSource:"conference" to EVERY link-bearing row) x packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/calendar-client.ts mergeOccurrence (!same && !newer => unresolved contradictory-revision; semantic() includes the new key) x schedule-state.ts prepareWebinarSourceState (production webinar-release path)
evidence: Probe through the real functions: tick 1 prepareWebinarSourceState with an acquisition from the pre-unit mapper shape (hangoutLink event, no meetingUrlSource, updated 2026-09-30T10:00:00.000Z) -> state persisted, calendarEvents [w1]. Tick 2 with the cycle-1 mapper output (identical event, same updated, meetingUrlSource:conference) -> {events:[], inventoryReasons:[contradictory-revision], transitions:[unresolved]}; tick 3 same -> still dropped; only an edit (newer updated) clears it (tick 4 -> [w1]). Via reconcileWebinarSources directly: scope absent (legacy) -> events [] AND newStartsBlocked true for ALL events; scope available -> that event dropped. The same happens for a persisted event with no link whose text now yields a free-text link (inherent to T-036, safe direction). Default parity as claimed by the manifest (byte-identical selection) holds only for selectAutoRecordItems, not for the persisted-state comparison.
fix_direction: Make the field not change the persisted comparison for existing rows: either (a) the mapper omits meetingUrlSource for conference (missing = conference is already the documented rule; add it only for location/description) and update the contract/tests, or (b) semantic()/mergeOccurrence treat a missing meetingUrlSource on a url-bearing snapshot as conference. Add a test: persisted state without the field + same-revision event with meetingUrlSource:conference => event still scheduled, no unresolved, no transition. Also confirm no active recording is stopped by the transition.

area: scripts/webinar/skip-reason-vocabulary.test.mjs:12,20-26 (asserts length 14 and items.length 15); packages/meeting-bot/src/alert-who-production.test.ts (main only: fixture must cover every SKIP_REASONS value and EXPECTED[reason] must exist)

title: No test pins the client allow-list seam: a mutation that DROPS an invalid meetingUrlSource (so the normaliser reads it as missing = conference) survives the lane suite
evidence: Mutation: after text(input.meetingUrlSource,32) add delete input.meetingUrlSource when the value is not one of location/description/conference. Extractor 17, differential 3, calendar 15, auto-join 39, webinar-policy 19 all pass (SURVIVED). Only the checker probe (reconcileWebinarSources with values Description, desc, empty string, whitespace-padded conference, 32-char string, then selectAutoRecordItems: 0 scheduled) kills it. Code as written is correct (non-strings and control characters fail closed; any other string is kept and judged untrusted).
fix_direction: Add the probe loop to calendar-client/auto-join tests: variants [Description, desc, empty, location, " conference", conference + space, Conference, 32-char, 33-char (rejected), 1, null, [description]] x everyWebinar true/false through reconcileWebinarSources then selectAutoRecordItems: never scheduled.

title: Two selection paths do not read meetingUrlSource: the attendance selector in run-pipeline and the exported selectEventsToAutoJoin
area: scripts/webinar/calendar-attendance-policy.mjs selectVerifiedCalendarMeetings; packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/auto-join.ts selectEventsToAutoJoin (roadmap T-038 plans to feed it to record)
evidence: Attendance path: a description-link event mapped by the API has fingerprint unequal to the raw observation (raw url is conference data only), so it is skipped needs-review; if an observation matched it would be scheduled (forced probe). So the shield is incidental to the fingerprint, not a source check. selectEventsToAutoJoin has no provenance check and no production caller today.
fix_direction: When either path is wired or changed, require meetingUrlSource absent or conference before scheduling.

title: An outsider invite whose description/location repeats a legitimate meeting link and start time makes the legitimate conference event unresolved (ambiguous-identity), so it is not auto-recorded
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/calendar-client.ts reconcileWebinarSources (aliasOwners / ambiguous-identity) fed by free-text rows whose aliases come from normalizeOccurrence regardless of meetingUrlSource
evidence: Through the real mapper and prepareWebinarSourceState (available scope, the production path): events [legit: organizer host@good.com, hangoutLink https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij] -> calendarEvents [legit], scheduled [legit]. Events [legit, evil: organizer attacker@evil.com, same start/end, description Join https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij] -> calendarEvents [], inventory [ambiguous-identity, ambiguous-identity], transitions [unresolved, unresolved], scheduled []. Either order. With legacy (non-available) scope the same collision sets newStartsBlocked for ALL events. Before T-036 the outsider event had no link and no alias. Needs only that the outsider knows the meeting URL and start (true for public webinars, the purpose of this system) and that the invite reaches the calendar. Not introduced by cycle 2 but missed in cycles 0 and 1; cycle 2 leaves it. Gmail rows cannot do this (a Gmail row linked to a conference event does not downgrade or block it: tested; same-meeting Gmail row is skipped duplicate-session).
fix_direction: Rows whose meetingUrlSource is present and not conference contribute NO aliases (aliases: [] in normalizeOccurrence), so they can neither make a trusted event ambiguous nor link to Gmail rows; they stay visible as skipped unverified-link-source. Test: legit conference + outsider same-meeting/same-start event => legit still in calendarEvents and scheduled, no unresolved, no transition, in both scopes; and reverse order.

title: A cancelled calendar tombstone with an unknown id (an outsider can send then cancel an invite) is unknown-tombstone: it blocks all new starts under the legacy scope and marks every unlinked Gmail row unproven-calendar-history under the available scope
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/calendar-client.ts reconcileWebinarSources (unknown-tombstone, newStartsBlocked, orphan -> unproven-calendar-history). Identical at 8520fa8; not introduced or widened by T-036.
evidence: Same scenario on the pre-unit calendar-client.ts (8520fa8, loaded as a temp module) and on ced676f: calendar c0 (conference) + Gmail g0 (approved), one acquisition. Legacy scope: base cal=[c0] gmail=[g0] blocked=false; adding any cancelled unknown-id row (minimal tombstone with only id/cancelled, a cancelled invite with details, or one with a free-text link) gives cal=[] gmail=[] newStartsBlocked=true on BOTH versions. Available scope: cal=[c0], gmail=[] (g0 unresolved unproven-calendar-history) on BOTH. Reachability: an organiser sends an invite then cancels it before the client has seen it; the next sync returns it as cancelled with an unknown id. The state-clearing path (newer revision) is not available to the victim.
fix_direction: Separate the cases: a cancelled row for an event the client never accepted need not make history unproven for unrelated meetings; at least scope the block to rows sharing the tombstone alias or, for events from other organisers, record it without setting orphan. Needs an Approver decision on how conservative the unknown-tombstone rule must be (it exists to avoid missing a cancellation of a recording).
owner_decision: Approver decision D-159 (2026-10-13, supersedes D-154): tombstone retention 30 days (code MATCHED_HORIZON_MS, unchanged) and match window +/-24 h; code already matches. Row left open: its remaining item is not only the constants.
